title: Istradefylline in WWOX-LoF
summary: An adenosine comparison for post-burst propagation and preserved inhibition.

graph.evidence: A mouse hyperoxia challenge showed fewer motor seizures.
graph.inference: Receptor binding, seizure timing and tissue protection are separate endpoints.
graph.hypothesis: A2A can facilitate late propagation while A1 supplies a parallel brake.
graph.experiment: Match the first burst, verify target engagement and measure A1 function.

evidence: In a 30-minute hyperoxia challenge, motor seizures occurred in 1 of 6 treated and 6 of 6 control mice. In the separate kainate study, the drug-specific EEG comparison tested a P2X7 antagonist.
inference: Adult PET establishes striatal engagement. Reported recombinant affinities differ 12.5-fold between A2A and A2B. An illustrative equilibrium model predicts appreciable A2B occupancy when A2A occupancy is high.
hypothesis: Selectively reducing episode-dependent A2A gain could limit late WWOX propagation while preserving native A1 inhibition. ADORA2A RNA changes in opposite directions in mouse cortex and human organoids.
experiment: At measured local parent and adenosine, match first recruitment and compare recurrence with A2A occlusion and an A2B control. Read evoked A1 and inhibitory reserve.
limits: Juvenile exposure, native cortical target engagement and spontaneous WWOX electrographic effects are unresolved. Retain as a conditional research probe and defer systemic pediatric prioritization.
